top_stories.title: AI didn't kill academic publishing. It exposed the body
top_stories.summary: A commentary piece argues that generative AI has not destroyed academic publishing but has instead laid bare pre-existing structural weaknesses in the industry. The article examines how AI is accelerating and exposing longstanding problems around research integrity, peer review, and publication models. It raises questions about the future direction of scholarly communication in the AI era.

top_stories.title: Why Academic Publishing Needs Purpose-Built AI, Not Just General LLMs
top_stories.summary: This piece makes the case that general-purpose large language models are insufficient for the specific demands of academic publishing, and that the sector requires purpose-built AI tools tailored to its workflows and standards. It highlights the risks of applying off-the-shelf AI to tasks such as peer review, manuscript evaluation, and research discovery. The argument centres on the need for domain-specific design to ensure accuracy and research integrity.

top_stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg tells staff that AI agents haven't progressed enough
top_stories.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has told employees that AI agents have not advanced as quickly as he had hoped, according to TechCrunch. The remarks signal internal frustration at Meta about the pace of agentic AI development. The disclosure adds context to Meta's ongoing investment in AI infrastructure and its broader AI product strategy.

top_stories.title: Researchers need dedicated tools, not "off the shelf" AI - LSE
top_stories.summary: The London School of Economics argues that academic researchers require AI tools specifically designed for research contexts, rather than general consumer-facing products. The piece contends that off-the-shelf AI tools carry risks around accuracy, bias, and fitness for purpose when applied to scholarly work. It calls for greater investment in purpose-built research AI that meets the rigorous standards of academic inquiry.

top_stories.title: LinqAlpha raises US$22 million to expand AI agents for public-market research
top_stories.summary: LinqAlpha has secured $22 million in funding to grow its AI agent platform focused on public equity market research. The company aims to use the capital to expand its tools that automate and enhance investment research workflows. The raise reflects continued investor appetite for AI applications in financial services and market analysis.

further_links.title: Some of the nation's rich are letting AI teach their kids
further_links.summary: Wealthy families in the US are turning to AI-powered education platforms such as Alpha and Forge Prep to tutor their children, raising questions about equity and the future of elite schooling.

further_links.title: These celebrities are protecting their likenesses from AI — one trademark at a time
further_links.summary: Public figures are increasingly using trademark law as a tool to protect their voices, faces, and personas from unauthorised AI-generated reproductions.

further_links.title: AI turns data center power into an enterprise challenge
further_links.summary: Growing AI workloads are creating significant power supply and energy management challenges for enterprise data centres, with organisations struggling to meet rising compute demands.

further_links.title: AI ambitions expose software fragmentation, Zoho says
further_links.summary: Zoho warns that businesses pursuing AI adoption are being held back by fragmented software ecosystems that prevent effective AI integration across enterprise operations.

further_links.title: Forbes 2026 AI 50 List | Top Artificial Intelligence Companies
further_links.summary: Forbes has published its annual AI 50 list highlighting the most promising private artificial intelligence companies of 2026.

further_links.title: Al Vigier: Canada's AI strategy shouldn't include secret Palantir bills
further_links.summary: A commentary piece argues that Canada's national AI strategy should not involve undisclosed government contracts with data analytics firm Palantir, raising concerns about transparency and AI governance.

further_links.title: Zoho: SMEs must digitize before adopting AI
further_links.summary: Zoho argues that small and medium-sized enterprises need to complete foundational digital transformation before they can meaningfully benefit from AI adoption.

further_links.title: Infuriating Google commercial imagines the founding fathers embracing AI
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on a widely criticised Google advertisement that depicts the American founding fathers enthusiastically using AI tools, drawing a backlash over its portrayal of AI adoption.

further_links.title: A sociotechnical threat model for AI-driven smart home devices
further_links.summary: Researchers have published an arXiv paper proposing a sociotechnical threat model for AI-enabled smart home devices, examining security, privacy, and social risks associated with their deployment.

further_links.title: Top Companies Driving Innovation in AI-Powered Education
further_links.summary: A market overview examines key companies, including Carnegie Learning, that are shaping the rapidly expanding AI-powered education sector.
